'''Brian Joshua Cook''' (born December 4, 1980) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He was drafted out of the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign|University of Illinois]] with the 24th overall pick in the [[2003 NBA draft]] by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].

In 2004, Cook was named to the [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball#All-Century Team|University of Illinois All-Century Team]].<ref>[http://archives.lincolndailynews.com/2004/Oct/18/News_new/sports_e.shtml Cook named to the All-Century Team]</ref>

==High school career==
Cook played high school basketball at [[Lincoln Community High School]] in central Illinois where he led the Railsplitters to the quarterfinals of the 1999 [[Illinois High School Association]] class AA state boys basketball tournament. Cook scored 38 points in 2 [[Illinois High School Boys Basketball Championship|IHSA tournament]] finals games, averaging 19.0 points per game.<ref>[https://www.ihsa.org/archive/bkb/mm/1999baa2.htm IHSA.org/Archive]</ref> He was named to the 1998 [[State Farm Holiday Classic]] all-tournament team and was a [[1999 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|1999 McDonald's All-American]]. He was also named the 1999 [[Illinois Mr. Basketball]] after averaging 21.7 points, 10.1 rebounds, 3.2 blocks, 2.0 steals and 1.8 assists per game as a senior.<ref name=bio>[http://www.fightingillini.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/cook_brian00.html Brian Cook Bio] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006081322/http://www.fightingillini.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/cook_brian00.html |date=October 6, 2014 }}</ref> Cook was inducted into the Illinois Basketball Coaches Association Hall of Fame in 2016.<ref>[http://basketballmuseumofillinois.com/hall-of-fame/players/19-hof-players/489-brian-cook BasketballMuseumofIllinois.com]</ref>

==College career==

Cook played 132 games in four years for the University of Illinois, most of them under coach [[Bill Self]], and led the Illini in [[rebound (basketball)|rebounding]] in each season. Cook was a versatile scorer from both inside and outside the paint, utilizing his height to score in the post and hitting three-point shots when left open. This helped him to earn co-Big Ten Freshman of the Year honors during his freshman year at Illinois.

Cook helped lead the Illini to a number one seed in the 2001 NCAA Tournament, and the Illini cruised to the Elite 8, where they were upset in a hard-fought and controversial game by Cook's future teammate [[Luke Walton]] and the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]].

As a senior in the 2002–03 season, Cook led the Fighting Illini in scoring with 20.0 points per game, and received the [[Chicago Tribune Silver Basketball]] as the [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Most Outstanding Player]] of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. That same season, Cook was named second team All-American by [[The Sporting News]], and third team All-American by the [[Associated Press]], the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]], and ''The Basketball Times'', as well as Big Ten Player of the Year and first team All-Big Ten by both the coaches and the media. Additionally, he would lead the Illini to the [[Big Ten men's basketball tournament]] championship and be named [[Big Ten tournament Most Outstanding Player|Most Outstanding Player]]. Cook left Illinois as the school's third all-time leading scorer with 1,748 total points, at an average of 13.2 points per game, behind [[Deon Thomas]] and [[Kiwane Garris]].<ref name="bio" /><ref>[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/brian-cook-1.html Brian Cook Stats] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006120105/http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/brian-cook-1.html |date=October 6, 2014 }}</ref>

==Professional career==
[[File:Brian Cook.jpg|thumb|upright|Cook with the Los Angeles Lakers]]
Cook was selected with the 24th overall pick in the [[2003 NBA draft]] by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. He played sparingly in his rookie campaign as a backup to superstar center [[Shaquille O'Neal]], and was mostly an interior player, notching only five three-point attempts out of 141 total field goal attempts. As his professional career evolved, however, Cook once again became a player who could play beyond the perimeter, after O'Neal moved on to the [[Miami Heat]] and [[Rudy Tomjanovich]] took over for [[Phil Jackson]] as Lakers' head coach. He was mainly used as a [[three-point field goal|three-point]] specialist; 199 of 422 (or 47.2%) of Cook's field goal attempts were from behind the three-point arc. When Phil Jackson returned to coach the Lakers in 2005–06, Cook started to take less three-pointers again, which resulted in Cook improving his overall field-goal percentage from .417 in 2004–05 to .520 in 2005–06. It also resulted in an improvement in his three-point field-goal percentage, from .392 in 2004–05 to .441 in 2005–06. His improved play kept Cook on the court more as his minutes played per game rose from 15.1 in 2004–05 to 19.4 in 2005–06.

On November 20, 2007, Cook was traded, along with [[Maurice Evans (basketball)|Maurice Evans]], to the [[Orlando Magic]] in exchange for [[Trevor Ariza]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/magic/news/Magic_Acquire_Brian_Cook_and_M-244872-66.html Magic Acquire Brian Cook and Maurice Evans From L.A. Lakers]</ref>

On February 19, 2009, Cook was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in a three-team trade also involving the Magic and the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=3539 | title = Magic get Rafer Alston in 3-team trade involving Grizzlies, Rockets, Kyle Lowry, others | work = InsideHoops.com | date = February 19, 2009 | access-date = July 23, 2013}}</ref> On February 20, 2010, he was waived by the Rockets.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=5439 |title=Rockets waive Brian Cook, keep Garrett Temple 10 more days |access-date=July 24, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160925011102/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=5439 |archive-date=September 25, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On July 9, 2010, Cook signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/breakingnews_cook_100709.html | title = CLIPPERS SIGN FREE AGENT FORWARD BRIAN COOK | work = NBA.com | date = July 9, 2010 | access-date = July 23, 2013}}</ref>

On March 15, 2012, Cook was traded, along with a 2015 second-round pick, to the [[Washington Wizards]] in exchange for [[Nick Young (basketball)|Nick Young]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards_acquire_nene_031512.html|title=WIZARDS ACQUIRE NENE FROM DENVER|date=March 15, 2012|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=March 17, 2012}}</ref>

Cook's final NBA game ever was during his time with the Wizards, as he played his final game on April 26, 2012, in a 104–70 win over the [[Miami Heat]]. He recorded 4 points and 1 rebound in his final game. On September 17, 2012, he re-signed with the Wizards. However, he was later waived by the Wizards on October 28, 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-waive-cook-and-mack|title=Wizards Waive Cook and Mack|work=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2012|access-date=July 23, 2013}}</ref>

In March 2013, Cook signed with [[Piratas de Quebradillas]] for the 2013 [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|BSN]] season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/99665/piratas-de-quebradillas-set-to-sign-brian-cook.html Piratas de Quebradillas set to sign Brian Cook]</ref><ref>[http://www.primerahora.com/deportes/baloncesto/nota/piratasfirmanabriancook-800724/ Piratas firman a Brian Cook] {{in lang|es}}</ref>

On September 30, 2013, Cook signed with the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-signs-three-free-agents-0 Utah Jazz Signs Three Free Agents]</ref> However, he was later waived by the Jazz on October 26, 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14657 |title=Utah Jazz waive Brian Cook, Dominic McGuire, Justin Holiday, Lester Hudson and Scott Machado |access-date=October 27, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006102942/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14657 |archive-date=October 6, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On September 25, 2014, Cook signed with the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref name="b068">{{cite web | title=Detroit Pistons Sign Four to Training Camp Roster | website=NBA.com | date=2014-09-25 | url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-four-training-camp-roster | access-date=2025-02-11}}</ref> However, he was later waived by the Pistons on October 20, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2014/news/10/20/pistons-moves.ap/index.html |title=Pistons release Thabeet, three others |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=October 21, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141209044246/http://www.nba.com/2014/news/10/20/pistons-moves.ap/index.html |archive-date=December 9, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On December 28, 2014, he signed with [[Sporting Al Riyadi Beirut|Al-Riyadi]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/146488/former-nba-forward-brian-cook-signs-with-riyadi.html Former NBA forward Brian Cook signs with Riyadi]</ref> He left Al-Riyadi in mid-January after appearing in just three games. On February 10, 2015, he signed with Aguada of the [[Liga Uruguaya de Basketball]], in [[Montevideo]], Uruguay.<ref>[http://www.futbol.com.uy/auc.aspx?261609,1045 Conocé al nuevo extranjero de Aguada]</ref> He also managed just three games for Aguada.

On June 15, 2015, Cook signed with [[Chiba Jets]] of the Japanese [[National Basketball League (Japan)|National Basketball League]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/163997/brian-cook-signs-in-japan-with-chiba-jets.html Brian Cook signs in Japan with Chiba Jets]</ref>

==Personal life==
Cook is the son of [[Norm Cook|Norman]] and Joyce Cook, and has two younger sisters, Kristina and Natasha. His father was an All-American with the [[University of Kansas]] and played briefly for the [[Boston Celtics]]. His uncle, Joe Cook, played basketball for [[Duke University]] from 1988 to 1990.<ref name="bio" />

On July 4, 2009, Cook married long-time girlfriend, Victoria Velasquez.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20090707040226/http://www.people.com/people/article/0,,20289496,00.html Basketball Star Brian Cook Weds]</ref>

Cook has played in the [[BIG3]] basketball league as a member of the [[Killer 3's]] team.
